html:
Cai Lun was a eunuch official at the court of the Eastern Han dynasty, credited with making paper cheap and good enough for everyday writing.

He entered the palace as a young man and rose under Emperor He, becoming head of the imperial workshops, which made weapons and fine goods for the court. In 105 he presented the emperor with a new kind of paper, made from tree bark, hemp, old rags and fishing nets, beaten into pulp (Cai Lun's papermaking). Paper already existed, but it was rough and used mainly for wrapping; books were written on bamboo strips or costly silk.

Cai Lun was also caught up in palace politics, close to the powerful Empress Deng. After her death in 121 a new emperor ordered him to report to prison, and he took poison instead.

His paper spread across China and later to Korea, Japan, and through Samarkand to the Islamic world and Europe. For this he is often counted among the most influential people in history.
sum: Cai Lun was a eunuch official at the court of the Eastern Han dynasty, credited with making paper cheap and good enough for everyday writing.
